messages:
customer_acct: Hey, invoice jumped massively this billing cycle — our SDK estimator shows ~2k tokens per run but the invoice shows ~20k per run. We stream and upload a file via multipart. Repro curl below, minimal. Can someone help?

customer_acct: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'X-Service-Meta: {"org":"acme","project":"ingest","user":"1234"}' \
  -F 'model=redwood-large' \
  -F 'messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this"}]' \
  -F 'file=@payload.json'
```

jessica_support: Thanks — can you confirm SDK version, streaming=true/false, and whether you use function calls? Also sample request_ts if you have one.

customer_acct: SDK 1.4.2, streaming=true, we call function summarize_file and we pass only a file_id in the function args (we thought the actual blob was not sent to the model). No obvious big completion text.

matt_engineer: Two quick hypotheses: (1) an ingress sidecar/materializer is expanding X-Service-Meta or headers into a system message, (2) the multipart/file blob got inlined (base64) into the model input. Either would massively increase token counts and would be charged by server metering. We'll check server request logs.

proxy-bot: ingress: found header x-service-meta on 83% of tenant requests. Rule "materialize-metadata" is active and expands header into an initial system message for POST /v1/chat/completions.

sam_billing: FYI metering: we tokenize the server-side request payload (system + messages + tool args) as the canonical source. Local SDK estimators only know client-side prompt + completion and do NOT see proxy-side materialization or server blob inlining. That explains a lot of cases where customers undercount vs invoice.

jessica_support: Can we pull a sample server request body for a single run so the customer can see what was actually tokenized? matt, can you paste an anonymized excerpt?

matt_engineer: Log excerpt (sanitized):
```
{
  "model": "redwood-large",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"tenant_meta: {\"org\":\"acme\",\"project\":\"ingest\",\"user\":\"1234\"}"},
    {"role":"user","content":"Summarize this"}
  ],
  "function_call": {
    "name": "summarize_file",
    "arguments": {
      "file_id": "abc-123",
      "blob_base64": "[BASE64 PAYLOAD ~40000 chars]"
    }
  }
}
```

customer_acct: Wait — where did blob_base64 come from? We only passed file_id.

matt_engineer: Ingress was configured to fetch the file by id and inline the blob into the function args to simplify sync function handling. That fetch+inline happened before metering, so the full base64 is what got tokenized and billed. The SDK estimator never saw that inline blob (it only counted the file_id).

jessica_support: Actionable recs: (a) Disable the materialization rule for your tenant so headers aren't injected into the system prompt, (b) change the proxy to pass a pointer to the blob rather than inlining base64 into function args (or perform server-side tool execution outside the model request), (c) we'll assess invoice delta and propose credit if this caused the spike.

customer_acct: Please do. Also can you add a small explainer to docs about estimator caveats (proxies, multipart, server-side fetches) so we don't get blind spots?

jessica_support: Will do. TL;DR: SDK estimators do not account for proxy-side injections or server-side materialization/inlining. For multipart or file workflows trust server audit logs for billing reconciliation. I'll follow up with credit ETA and a docs PR. :thumbsup:
